title: COPY/ADD --chmod rejects symbolic modes (only octal accepted) — BuildKit parity gap
body:
## Summary

buildah's `COPY --chmod` / `ADD --chmod` accepts **octal numeric modes only**. It rejects all **symbolic** modes (`u+x`, `go-w`, `a+rX`, `a+rX,go-w`, …) and the Go `0o755` prefix, all of which BuildKit accepts. This breaks building Dockerfiles that use BuildKit-style symbolic `--chmod` — an increasingly common pattern.

## Empirical results

Minimal repro:
```
printf 'FROM scratch\nCOPY --chmod=<MODE> ctx.txt /ctx.txt\n' > Dockerfile && podman build .
```

buildah `1.44.0` (podman 6.0.0 server):

| `--chmod=` | result |
|---|---|
| `0755`, `0644` | ✅ accepted |
| `0o755` | ❌ rejected |
| `a+rx`, `a+rwx` | ❌ rejected |
| `u+x` | ❌ rejected |
| `go-w` | ❌ rejected |
| `a+rX` | ❌ rejected |
| `a+rX,go-w`, `u+rX,go-w` | ❌ rejected |

Only plain octal (no `0o` prefix) is accepted. Every symbolic form — including the simple `u+x` — fails during `COPY`/`ADD` with `Error parsing chmod <mode>`.

## Impact

Dockerfiles using BuildKit-style symbolic `--chmod` cannot be built with buildah/podman. Real example: `COPY --link --chmod=a+rX,go-w . .`, which projects use to set "readable + traversable by non-root, no group/other write" in one layer instead of a separate `chmod -R` pass over a large tree.

The workaround is to rewrite the mode to octal, but that (a) must be reapplied per build, and (b) is not always a 1:1 conversion — symbolic modes like `a+rX` are *conditional* on each file's existing mode (capital `X` = "execute only for dirs / already-executable files"), so a fixed octal constant is a lossy approximation.

## Request

Support symbolic `--chmod` modes in `COPY`/`ADD` for BuildKit parity, resolving each clause against the copied file's current mode (as BuildKit does). Even partial support for the common `a`/`u`/`g`/`o` ± `r`/`w`/`x`/`X` forms would unblock most real-world Dockerfiles.

## Environment

- buildah `1.44.0` (podman `6.0.0` server, macOS applehv machine)
- BuildKit (Docker buildx) accepts all the rejected forms

comments.body: AFAICT that was fixed recently in main https://github.com/podman-container-tools/buildah/commit/b0751fc6b83977e29c237eabf17849866edad1e2 and should be part of the next release 1.45

## Summary

#6938 (*"COPY/ADD --chmod rejects symbolic modes (only octal accepted) — BuildKit parity
gap"*) was closed on 2026-07-06 as already-fixed, citing commit `b0751fc6b` and expected in
release 1.45:

> AFAICT that was fixed recently in main
> https://github.com/podman-container-tools/buildah/commit/b0751fc6b83977e29c237eabf17849866edad1e2
> and should be part of the next release 1.45

That commit is real and correct, but it fixed a **different surface**. The Containerfile
`COPY --chmod=` / `ADD --chmod=` instruction path is still octal-only on current `main`.

## What `b0751fc6b` actually fixed

PR #6778 ("Add support for symbolic chmod options", **Fixes #6066**) adds a `Chmod string`
option to `GetOptions`/`PutOptions` in `copier`, wired through `add.go`, using
`github.com/tonistiigi/dchapes-mode`. Its own commit message scopes it precisely:

> This adds an optional Chmod string option to GetOptions and PutOptions. If set, this
> overrides the ChmodDirs and ChmodFiles options. If unset, they continue to work as before.
>
> **The --chmod option to buildah add and buildah copy works with symbolic as well as
> numeric arguments.**

So `buildah add --chmod=+x` and `buildah copy --chmod=+x` — the **CLI subcommands** — now
accept symbolic modes. The Containerfile instruction does not.

## Why the instruction path is unaffected

`COPY --chmod=` / `ADD --chmod=` is validated **at parse time**, before buildah's executor
ever sees the value, by the vendored `openshift/imagebuilder`:

`vendor/github.com/openshift/imagebuilder/dispatchers.go:817-825`

```go
// checkChmodConversion makes sure that the argument to a --chmod= flag for
// COPY or ADD is an octal number
func checkChmodConversion(chmod string) error {
	_, err := strconv.ParseUint(chmod, 8, 32)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("Error parsing chmod %s", chmod)
	}
	return nil
}
```

Called from the COPY dispatcher at `dispatchers.go:269-273` and the ADD dispatcher at
`dispatchers.go:188-193`. Since it rejects at dispatch, none of #6778's plumbing is reachable
for the instruction form.

buildah `1.46.0-dev` vendors `openshift/imagebuilder v1.2.21`, which still contains the
octal-only check.

## Reproduction on the released 1.45.0

Tested on **buildah 1.45.0** — the exact release the fix was expected in:

```console
$ buildah version | head -1
Version:         1.45.0

$ echo hi > script.sh

$ printf 'FROM scratch\nCOPY --chmod=0755 script.sh /script.sh\n' > Containerfile.octal
$ buildah build --no-cache -f Containerfile.octal -t t-octal .
Successfully tagged localhost/t-octal:latest          # ✅ octal still fine

$ printf 'FROM scratch\nCOPY --chmod=+x script.sh /script.sh\n' > Containerfile.symbolic
$ buildah build --no-cache -f Containerfile.symbolic -t t-sym .
STEP 1/2: FROM scratch
STEP 2/2: COPY --chmod=+x script.sh /script.sh
Error: building at STEP "COPY --chmod=+x script.sh /script.sh": Error parsing chmod +x

$ printf 'FROM scratch\nCOPY --chmod=u+x,go-w script.sh /script.sh\n' > Containerfile.sym2
$ buildah build --no-cache -f Containerfile.sym2 -t t-sym2 .
Error: building at STEP "COPY --chmod=u+x,go-w script.sh /script.sh": Error parsing chmod u+x,go-w
```

This matches the empirical matrix in the original #6938 report exactly — nothing in that
table has changed.

### The asymmetry, side by side

The same symbolic mode that fails as an instruction **succeeds** as a CLI subcommand on the
very same binary, which is precisely the surface #6778 fixed:

```console
$ c=$(buildah from scratch)
$ buildah copy --chmod=+x "$c" script.sh /script.sh
c8e4eb0c2d2c2ba375b107c5298693527d2706c53c84183bcb5982374f0118e3   # ✅ exit 0
```

Additionally driving the vendored parser directly on current `main` (`b544ad829`) —
`ParseDockerfile` → `NewStages` → `Step.Resolve` → `Builder.Run` — confirms rejection happens
at dispatch, before buildah's executor is reached:

```
COPY --chmod=0755 a /b        ACCEPTED
COPY --chmod=+x a /b          REJECTED: Error parsing chmod +x
COPY --chmod=u+x,go-w a /b    REJECTED: Error parsing chmod u+x,go-w
ADD  --chmod=a+rX a /b        REJECTED: Error parsing chmod a+rX
COPY --chmod=0o755 a /b       REJECTED: Error parsing chmod 0o755
```

## Scope of the remaining fix

1. Relax or remove `checkChmodConversion` in `openshift/imagebuilder` so symbolic modes reach
   buildah (an imagebuilder PR + revendor is required — this cannot be fixed in buildah alone).
2. Plumb the string through `stage_executor.Copy` into the `AddAndCopyOptions.Chmod` path that
   #6778 already made symbolic-aware.

Item 2 is largely done; item 1 is the blocker.

## Related / duplicates still open

- [containers/podman#28293](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/28293) —
  *"Error parsing chmod +x in ADD/COPY instructions"* — **still open**, and tracking exactly
  this instruction-level gap.
- #6732 references it under the `ModeStr` checklist entry, recommending
  `tonistiigi/dchapes-mode` — the same library #6778 used.
- #6066 (closed by #6778) and #4614 (closed 2023 without a fix) are the earlier rounds; both
  were reported against the **Containerfile** form, which suggests #6066 may also have been
  closed against the wrong surface.
- #2961 → #3004 (2021) is the original octal-only implementation that created the gap.

## Parity context

Symbolic `--chmod` was labs-only in the BuildKit Dockerfile frontend from **1.11.0** and
**graduated to stable in 1.14.0** (2025-02-19). It is no longer a labs-gated feature, so
Containerfiles using it are mainstream rather than opt-in.

Following up on the repro above: this is now fixed at the root cause, in the layer that owns the check.

The blocker was (and on buildah `main` still is) `checkChmodConversion` in the vendored `openshift/imagebuilder`: it validates `--chmod=` at dispatch time with `strconv.ParseUint` (octal only), so symbolic values are rejected before buildah's executor, which is already symbolic-aware (that is what b0751fc6b/#6778 wired up), ever sees them.

PR: **openshift/imagebuilder#324** (branch `copy-add-symbolic-chmod`)

What it does:

- `checkChmodConversion` accepts octal as before (now range-checked to 0-07777, as BuildKit's frontend does), and additionally validates symbolic modes by delegating to `mode.Parse` from `github.com/tonistiigi/dchapes-mode`: the library that owns this grammar (it is what buildah's executor uses to resolve these values, and what BuildKit's frontend uses). Deliberately not a local re-implementation of the grammar, because chmod(1) allows repeated op-perms groups within a clause (`u+r-w`), which a subset validator keeps getting wrong.
- The imagebuilder-internal `dockerclient` executor resolved `Chmod` octal-only and would have turned the newly-accepted values into a later, fuzzier error; it now resolves them with the same library, with the tar-header special bits (setuid/setgid/sticky) mapped correctly and unit-tested.
- The dependency is stdlib-only and already in imagebuilder's module graph via `moby/buildkit` v0.29.0.

Verified end-to-end with buildah `main` + that branch via a `replace` directive (Linux VM, `FROM scratch` builds, modes read back from the built layer):

| source mode | `--chmod=` | result |
|---|---|---|
| 700 | `a+rX,go-w` | 755 |
| 644 | `+x` | 755 |
| 644 | `u+x,go-w` | 744 |
| 700 | `u+rX-w` | 500 |
| 644 | `g+r=rx` | 654 |

Octal builds unchanged; `888`, `rwxrwxrwx`, `0o755`, and `17777` still rejected. The conditional `X` resolves per-file as expected (`a+rX` on a 0700 script yields 0755).

Once the imagebuilder PR lands and buildah revendors (I can send that PR, including a `bud` test, as soon as there is a revendorable commit), the instruction path is fixed with no buildah-side code change: the wiring from `Copy.Chmod` through `stage_executor` into `AddAndCopyOptions.Chmod` already exists on `main`.

Reopen candidate: the close reason ("fixed in main, 1.45") is disproven by the repro on released 1.45.0 above; the fix requires an imagebuilder change, which is exactly what this PR is.
